proposed.explanation:
Comparison of the four companies on net-profit growth (2024→2025) and trailing P/E (price ÷ 2025 EPS):

• ETEL (Telecom Egypt): Net profit fell from 10,111,328,000 EGP to 578,063,000 EGP, a decline of roughly 94 %. P/E on 2025 EPS (11.93) is 141.95/11.93 ≈ 11.9. A near-total collapse in earnings makes this a high-risk name for a medium-risk, long-term growth investor.

• COMI (CIB): Net profit rose from 55,256,732,000 EGP to 82,258,815,000 EGP, growth of ≈ 48.9 %. P/E on 2025 EPS (18.25) is 128.00/18.25 ≈ 7.0. This is the lowest multiple in the group combined with strong double-digit earnings growth.

• EFID (Edita): Net profit rose from 1,606,727,698 EGP to 2,695,301,670 EGP, growth of ≈ 67.8 %. P/E on 2025 EPS (2.18) is 20.40/2.18 ≈ 9.4. Highest growth rate, but the absolute earnings base is smaller and the stock is a lower-priced, more volatile name.

• TMGH (Talaat Moustafa): Net profit rose from 12,769,517,325 EGP to 18,201,981,482 EGP, growth of ≈ 42.5 %. P/E on 2025 EPS (6.98) is 82.50/6.98 ≈ 11.8. Solid growth but the richest multiple of the three growers.

Recommendation – Buy COMI (CIB), 312 shares at 128.00 EGP = 39,936 EGP.

Rationale: For a 7+ year growth horizon with medium risk tolerance, CIB offers the best risk-reward balance in this set. A P/E of about 7 means you are paying the least for each pound of current earnings, while the 49 % profit growth shows the earnings base is expanding. The banking sector provides a relatively stable cash-flow profile over a multi-year horizon. The other three either carry a much higher multiple (TMGH, EFID) or show a dramatic earnings collapse (ETEL).

Position sizing: 312 × 128 = 39,936 EGP, leaving 40,064 EGP cash. Total portfolio = 80,000 EGP; COMI represents 49.9 %, just under the 50 % single-name cap.

Risks and uncertainty: A P/E of 7 may reflect market concerns about the banking sector (interest-rate environment, credit quality, regulatory changes) that are not captured in the two-year profit figures. The 48.9 % growth is a single-year comparison; it may not repeat. ETEL's 94 % profit drop could signal a one-off charge or a structural problem, but the evidence does not clarify which. This is guidance, not a guarantee of returns. Consider adding a second position (e.g., EFID or TMGH) with the remaining cash in a future period to improve diversification.
